title: Array algorithms
description:
Complete the methods. None of them may change the arrays they are given.

```java
static int[] rotate(int[] values, int k)       // every item k places to the right, wrapping around; k may be negative or large
static int secondLargest(int[] values)         // the second-largest distinct value
static int[] runningTotals(int[] values)       // {1, 2, 3} gives {1, 3, 6}
static int[][] transpose(int[][] m)            // rows become columns
static int[] mergeSorted(int[] a, int[] b)     // two sorted arrays into one sorted array, in one pass
```

- `secondLargest({5, 9, 9, 2})` is 5. With fewer than two distinct values it throws `IllegalArgumentException`.
- `transpose` of a 2 × 3 matrix is 3 × 2. You may assume every row has the same length (and that there is at least one row).
hints: For `rotate`, item `i` moves to index `(i + shift) % n`, where `shift = Math.floorMod(k, n)` turns any `k` into 0 to n-1.
For `secondLargest`, keep the largest and second-largest seen so far in one pass; a value equal to the largest is not a new second.

To fail with an error, `throw new IllegalArgumentException("needs two distinct values");` stops the method at once (exceptions are covered fully in lesson 4.04). Starting `first` and `second` as `long` values below every `int`, like `Long.MIN_VALUE`, lets you tell "nothing found yet" apart from a real value.
rules: Merge in one pass and find the second largest without sorting.
